summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Umbragen through the Console's per-route usage and cost decomposition. Focus on tagging routes, mapping tokens to billable units, using Optimize suggestions (batching/caching) to reduce unit costs, and considerations for Dedicated vs Hosted for SLOs and data residency. Agreed next steps: share recording, pricing ranges, run sample billing export, and schedule infra deep-dive.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-10 14:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Sofia Malik (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Umbragen Head of Platform), Ethan Moore (FinOps), Lena Yu (SRE)

[00:00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood Inference. Diego and I will run through the Console demo, specifically the traffic-to-cost decomposition for per-route billing. Short agenda, then demo.
[00:00:12] Priya: Great, thanks. We have Ethan and Lena on - looking to understand how we split costs per customer-facing route, and whether we should go Dedicated or stay Hosted for now.
[00:00:25] Diego: Awesome, that's exactly what this view is for. Quick question before we start — what's your current setup? Are you sending requests through an API gateway with route metadata?
[00:00:35] Ethan: Right now it's our Kubernetes ingress + a sidecar that adds a route header. We also have an internal job doing aggregations for billing but it's pretty manual.
[00:00:45] Lena: Also curious about how the KV cache behaves across routes when we have multi-tenant inference, we want to avoid leakage.
[00:00:53] Sofia: Good callout. In the Console we surface per-route cache hits and prefix cache reuse, the defaults are tenant-isolated so KV cache keys are scoped. I'll show the visibility panels.
[00:01:07] Diego: Jumping into the Console — top left is the usage lens, you can filter by route label, by team, or by model. Here we have a sample app with two primary routes: short-chat and doc-qa.
[00:01:25] [00:01:25] Diego: Notice the 'route mapping' column, that maps the gateway header to a route id that you can use for billing exports.
[00:01:34] Priya: Looks clean. How granular are these tokens? We need to map tokens to cents level for chargebacks.
[00:01:42] Sofia: We export token counts per request, and the cost decomposition view attributes compute, IO, and infra overhead to tokens. There's also a per-token delta for cached tokens vs generated tokens.
[00:01:58] Ethan: Can we see an example where cache reduces cost?
[00:02:02] Diego: Yup — switching to the 'Optimize suggestions' tab. For doc-qa route we have a 23% token reuse via prefix caching. Console suggests enabling a 5s prefix cache and shorter model context for that route, which drops token spend by ~18% in this sample.
[00:02:20] [00:02:20] Priya: That's helpful. Our doc-qa route has a lot of repeated system prompts so this should hit. How about batching? We have bursty traffic but small requests.
[00:02:30] Diego: The recommendations engine suggests micro-batching at 50ms windows for that route — small enough to keep P95 latency within 200ms but increase token throughput and reduce per-token overhead.
[00:02:41] Lena: Are those auto-applied or just suggestions? We want control.
[00:02:45] Sofia: Suggestions only by default. You can apply a policy to auto-approve Optimize suggestions for non-critical routes. For critical routes you deploy via the rollout page.
[00:02:55] Ethan: Talk to me about Dedicated — if we go Dedicated does cost attribution still work the same?
[00:03:01] Diego: Yes — Dedicated is just reserved GPU capacity. The Console still collects route metadata, token counts, and does the same decomposition. The big differences are predictable throughput and private networking.
[00:03:13] Priya: We have compliance needs — SOC 2, SSO via SAML, and KMS for keys. Do you support on-prem KMS?
[00:03:23] Sofia: We integrate with customer KMS and HSM for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer managed KMS but can bring-your-own keys for Dedicated in most cases. Audit logs and long retention are available as an add-on.
[00:03:36] [00:03:36] Diego: Scrolling to the 'cost breakdown' panel — here's a route-level pie: compute, model licensing (if applicable), and infra overhead. You can export this as CSV or connect to your billing system via S3/ops webhook.
[00:03:51] Ethan: Nice. Can we see a sample CSV export? That's what our FinOps tools expect.
[00:03:56] Diego: Sure, I'm exporting now — it includes route_id, timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hits, cost_usd, model_version.
[00:04:10] [00:04:10] Priya: Small thing — sometimes our gateway strips headers, can we map routes by path pattern instead?
[00:04:18] Sofia: Yes — in route mapping you can set matchers by header, path regex, or even downstream microservice name. That gets stamped on the Console telemetry.
[00:04:30] Ethan: Competitors we've looked at had trouble splitting long calls that involve tool calls and function calling. How does Redwood show function/tool call tokenization?
[00:04:40] Diego: We break out tool call tokens separately and show them in the call trace. It helps separate model token spend from external tool invocation costs. There is sometimes noise in ASR transcriptions of function names but the telemetry ties to the request id.
[00:04:56] [00:04:56] Priya: Any gotchas with VPC/private network egress costs? We plan to keep data in our VPC.
[00:05:03] Sofia: In Private deployments the control plane can be in your VPC or we can peer; egress is minimized. We'll run a network sizing doc as a follow-up.
[00:05:13] Ethan: Let's talk numbers — rough unit cost per 1k tokens for your hosted Llama-like model?
[00:05:19] Sofia: It depends on model and sequence length. For open models in our catalog you can see per-token baselines in the model profile — ballpark $0.XX per 1k for smaller LLMs to $X.XX for larger ones. We'll send ranges.
[00:05:33] [00:05:33] Diego: Switching to an anomaly view — Console flags routes where cost per request spikes versus baseline. For example short-chat had a recent spike due to a context leakage bug; you can set alerts and automatically throttle or fallback to a cheaper model.
[00:05:48] Lena: Fallbacks are interesting. How are those configured?
[00:05:51] Diego: In routing policies you define priorities: model A, then model B fallback, then a degraded stateless path. You can also fallback by region if capacity is constrained.
[00:06:02] Priya: Do you store payloads? Our compliance team requires minimal retention.
[00:06:07] Sofia: By default we store minimal telemetry and token counts; you control retention for logs and full payloads. For Private you can opt out of payload retention entirely.
[00:06:18] [00:06:18] Ethan: Okay can you show me an actual customer example of a per-route billing playbook?
[00:06:22] Diego: I have an anonymized example — here a customer split tenants across routes and applied per-route quantization profiles. The results show a 32% reduction in unit costs on search routes with negligible quality loss.
[00:06:37] Priya: You said quantization profiles per route? That's helpful, we have quality-sensitive and cheap paths.
[00:06:42] Sofia: Exactly — you can pin quantization and model variants per route. Optimize suggests quantization levels and warns about estimated quality delta using eval sets.
[00:06:55] [00:06:55] Ethan: For the cost export we need route-level tags merged into our data warehouse. Is there a connector?
[00:07:02] Diego: Yes, S3 exports are common; we also have direct BigQuery/Redshift connectors in early access. For now CSV S3 is reliable and you can schedule hourly exports.
[00:07:14] Priya: Our main timeline is pilot next month and production in Q2. Are there sandbox limits?
[00:07:20] Sofia: For pilots we give reserved burst credits and a sandbox project. If you need Dedicated for Q2 we can start the procurement thread but pilot usually starts hosted.
[00:07:31] [00:07:31] Ethan: Procurement question — do you provide SOC 2 type II artifacts and network diagrams during vendor review?
[00:07:37] Sofia: Yes, we provide SOC 2 reports under NDA and a security pack. I'll attach the security checklist in the follow-up.
[00:07:46] Diego: Back to the console, showing the timeline — you can slice by dev/tag to see which team is driving costs, and set cost allocation rules for chargeback.
[00:07:57] Priya: If we want to roll out auto-Optimize suggestions for non-prod routes, how do we audit what changed?
[00:08:03] Diego: All Optimize actions produce a changelog entry with before/after expected spend and a confidence score. You can require manual approval if you want an audit gate.
[00:08:16] [00:08:16] Sofia: Quick live Q: Ethan, what's your largest monthly route today?
[00:08:20] Ethan: The chat assistant — about 3.2M requests, avg 120 tokens in.
[00:08:27] Diego: That's helpful. We can run a sample export that maps that traffic to expected spend under current config and with Optimize applied.
[00:08:36] Priya: That would help our procurement to justify Dedicated if savings are big.
[00:08:40] [00:08:40] Sofia: We're going to run that as a follow-up. Next I'll show the real-time alerting — you can set a P95 latency SLO and a cost per request threshold, and we will trigger a webhook to your ops topic.
[00:08:53] Ethan: Are webhooks guaranteed delivery? We use Kafka for reliability.
[00:08:57] Diego: We do retries and dead-letter to S3; we also support pushing to HTTP endpoints or SQS/Kafka via an enterprise connector.
[00:09:08] Priya: A couple of small usability asks — can the route mapping UI bulk-edit tags?
[00:09:13] Diego: Yes, bulk edit and import via CSV. Also we support regex-based transformations.
[00:09:20] [00:09:20] Lena: About KV cache again — you mentioned tenant scoping, do you also support shared caches for global prefix reuse? Our team sometimes wants cross-tenant knowledge.
[00:09:30] Sofia: You can configure cache scopes per route. Shared caches are opt-in and come with stricter review. We flag possible data leakage in the audit.
[00:09:43] Ethan: Any third-party costs we should be aware of when integrating? You mentioned model licensing earlier.
[00:09:48] Diego: If you bring a licensed proprietary model there may be licensing fees; our hosted catalog has models with known profiles. We'll include model licensing columns in the export so you can attribute those costs.
[00:09:59] [00:09:59] Priya: This is good. Can you show the rollout UI for applying a cost-reducing policy to a single route?
[00:10:05] Diego: Sure — creating a canary policy to enable micro-batching for doc-qa on 10% of traffic. You can watch the metrics and then promote to 100%. The Console will show expected cost delta.
[00:10:20] Sofia: Quick aside — sometimes transcriptions and function names get garbled in recordings; just FYI.
[00:10:25] Priya: Understood.
[00:10:28] [00:10:28] Diego: Fast-forwarding to the billing export — I've generated a sample CSV and pasted a link in the chat (https://redwood.example/demo/umbragen-sample-export.csv). It has route-level hourly rows.
[00:10:46] Ethan: Thanks — we'll ingest and compare against our internal numbers.
[00:10:51] Priya: On security: can you narrow SSO to certain user groups and enforce RBAC on the Console?
[00:10:58] Sofia: Yes, SAML groups map to RBAC roles. You can restrict cost views to FinOps, allow developers to see traces but not billing.
[00:11:09] Lena: What about audit log retention for compliance?
[00:11:12] Diego: We support configurable retention; for Private you can keep logs on-prem. For hosted we have tiered retention with add-on for long-term archival.
[00:11:23] [00:11:23] Ethan: Good. A couple of red flags from procurement: do you support termination data export? If we leave, can we get raw telemetry?
[00:11:30] Sofia: Yes — exit procedures include a full telemetry export and keys rotation. We'll include that in the SOW.
[00:11:38] Diego: Switching to the 'what-if' billing snapshot — I toggled Optimize suggestions on for doc-qa and quantization for search routes; the projection shows a 24% reduction in monthly spend for the demo dataset.
[00:11:55] Priya: Is there a way to simulate quality regressions? We need to be sure quantization doesn't harm queries.
[00:12:01] Diego: We run eval sets and show expected quality delta; you can upload your own eval prompts and Redwood will run quick comparisons.
[00:12:12] [00:12:12] Priya: Okay that's crucial. We'll prepare a small eval set.
[00:12:16] Sofia: Note: Diego will need the traffic CSV and a short list of SLOs.
[00:12:22] Ethan: I'll email the CSV tonight.
[00:12:25] [00:12:25] Diego: Quick demo note — we also show model warmup costs for cold KV cache and expected transient spikes; Console flags those in the timeline.
[00:12:36] Priya: If we move some routes to Dedicated, what are the lead times for that capacity?
[00:12:40] Sofia: Typical lead time is 4–6 weeks depending on GPU type and region; for high priority customers we can accelerate.
[00:12:51] [00:12:51] Priya: That's within our Q2 plan.
[00:12:54] Diego: A short Q: are there any internal billing mappings we should be aware of? Like do you include the infra overhead in the cost per token?
[00:13:01] Diego: Yes — infra overhead is included as a separate column and you can choose to amortize it across tokens or assign it to route owners.
[00:13:09] [00:13:09] Sofia: We're at about 12 minutes in — do you want to jump to a deeper ops question or keep browsing the Console?
[00:13:16] Priya: Let's do a quick ops deep-dive — Lena had specific network and cache questions.
[00:13:21] Diego: Great. Lena, you asked about cross-tenant KV scoping and network peering. For Private deployments we can deploy inference nodes into your VPC and ensure traffic never traverses our public networks. KV caches run inside the same infra and are bound to tenant ids.
[00:13:40] Lena: For autoscaling, how do you avoid noisy neighbor rescheduling affecting P95?
[00:13:46] Diego: We have GPU pool isolation options and autoscaler with priority bands. Critical routes can get pinned capacity. In Dedicated you can reserve pool lanes for specific customers.
[00:13:58] [00:13:58] Priya: What about data residency for EU customers? We have EU tenants.
[00:14:03] Sofia: We support region pinning and data residency controls; for hosted we have EU regions and for Private you can host on-prem or in a local cloud region.
[00:14:13] Ethan: Can we set budget alerts based on projected monthly run rate?
[00:14:16] Diego: Yes — Console supports projected spend alerts and will recommend Optimize actions to reduce run-rate if thresholds hit.
[00:14:25] [00:14:25] Priya: One more thing — our SREs want to see trace-level latency per token. Is that exposed?
[00:14:31] Diego: We expose per-request traces and token-level timing in the trace view. You can correlate to model, region, and queue time.
[00:14:41] Priya: That's perfect.
[00:14:44] [00:14:44] Sofia: Quick recap then next steps: we'll send recording + sample export link, Diego will run a billing projection against your CSV and produce a 2-scenario snapshot (hosted current config vs hosted+Optimize). We'll also share security docs and SOC2 under NDA.
[00:15:03] Ethan: Sounds good. Timeline: pilot next month, decision in Q2.
[00:15:09] Priya: Any pricing ballpark you'll send?
[00:15:13] Sofia: Yes ranges for hosted and a starting point for Dedicated commit tiers.
[00:15:20] [00:15:20] Diego: Last behavior demo — route-level reweighting: you can throttle dev routes during peak to protect production.
[00:15:28] Lena: Ok thanks. We'll follow up with the CSV and a list of routes we want to prioritize.
[00:15:34] Sofia: Awesome, we'll pick this up in the technical deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
[00:15:39] Priya: Thanks, this was very useful.
[00:15:42] Ethan: Thanks all.
[00:15:44] [00:15:44] End of recorded portion — Q&A offline and follow-up items noted.

Post-call notes (auto): Attendees requested a sample billing export and security pack. Diego to run workload projection. Action items captured in meeting metadata.

(Transcript contains minor transcription errors: e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, occasional speaker mislabels.)
